lines: +Verdicts rule first: any recorded reward > 0 is `policy`; a recorded 0 with a genuine trajectory is `policy` unless the clock/turns that produced it were materially consumed by the harness (below). No `result.json` means Harbor's `finally` never ran (hard kill) -> `harness`. Setup-phase failures (env/agent setup, broker create denied/quota, install/config errors) precede any policy action -> `harness`. Broker `sandbox_ended` with reason timeout/budget/shutdown/lost (or exited-137 without memory-hog commands), backend/Modal failures, LLM API/auth/connection errors, and `UnicodeDecodeError` (strict decode of terminal bytes is harness robustness) -> `harness`; best-effort `/logs/artifacts` read failures are ignored.

+AgentTimeouts are `policy` by default (uniform loaded-serving slowdown is not per-trial evidence). They flip to `harness` only with material clock theft: fabricated "Technical difficulties" turns (>=3 steps or >=10% of agent time — that string is a synthetic `LLMResponse` after context-overflow summarization fails, 0 policy tokens, so those episodes never happened); failed/spurious summarization residual time (>=50% of agent time unexplained by successful LLM calls + declared command waits + estimated truncations, with summarization log involvement — Harbor's token counter diverges from the server's, summarizations fire at a fraction of the real limit); a single unexplained stall >= max(180s, 25% of budget) versus run-level tokens/sec (observed: 610s for a 369-token reply); or a degraded sandbox in the broker audit (capture-pane excess, uniformly slow execs vs run median). Genuine format loops with substantive replies, output-truncation churn, long declared command waits, and sequence/output-length limit aborts after genuine work stay `policy`; first-turn prompt-too-long and empty-`content` loops whose text sits in `reasoning_content` (reasoning-parser/template mismatch — also applied run-wide when >=50% of trials never execute a command that way) are `harness`, because the policy's answer never reached the parser.

+Tmux/session death (`failed to send keys`, `no server running`) is `policy` when the sandbox stayed alive: in broker records the fatal keystrokes are the policy's own (`tmux kill-server`/`kill-session -t terminus-2`, `pkill bash`, `exit`, `C-d`, `exec`, source-exec) and Harbor would still have graded had the session ended at a turn boundary. Verifier timeouts are judged against same-task sibling verifier durations (median >=25% of budget -> `harness`, else the policy's artifact hung the tests -> `policy`; no completed siblings -> `harness`, as is a broker exec-cap kill of `test.sh`). Missing/unparsable reward files are `harness` unless the policy's own commands broke the verifier (chmod/mount/rm of tests or interpreters). For mini-swe-agent, Harbor drops the native `exit_status`, so the native trajectory/log are read: API/auth/rate-limit and binary crashes are `harness`, submitted/limit endings with a verdict, context/output-limit endings after genuine work, and safety refusals are `policy`; its timeouts default to `policy` absent LLM-error evidence.
